title: text_import: Handle multiple byte groups
description:
Have text2pcap and Import from Hex Dump support byte groups consisting
of 2 to 4 bytes in addition to individual bytes. By default assume
that byte groups are in network (big-endian) byte order, but add an
option to support little-endian byte order as produced by some hex dump
utilities.

Also support "0x" or "0X" before the hex offsets, as produced by
tcpdump -x

Fix #16193

notes.body:
From the [`text2pcap`](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/man-pages/text2pcap.html) man page:

> Any line beginning with #TEXT2PCAP is a directive and options can be inserted after this command to be processed by text2pcap. Currently there are no directives implemented; in the future, these may be used to give more fine grained control on the dump and the way it should be processed e.g. timestamps, encapsulation type etc.

Would adding a directive for specifying the endianness of the bytes be useful so the user doesn't necessarily need to worry about specifying the **--little-endian** option if `text2pcap` can automatically detect it from the new directive?  Obviously, if both were used, then one of them would have to take priority, likely **--little-endian**, in the event they conflicted.

I think it would be useful.

Possibly the directive should take priority? That would make it possible to do something like cat two hexdumps together, one Little Endian and one not, by including the directives in-band.

I was thinking that **--little-endian** would take precedence as a way to override the directive in the event that the directive was incorrect, but I haven't really given it that much thought to decide if that's a valid use case or not.  I do know that in many cases, specifying command-line options do override settings normally specified in configuration files - _sshd_ and `sshd_config` come to mind, for example.  But I defer to your good judgment.

Yeah, I can see either way. The directive would be in the data file itself, which I think perhaps is a good reason for it to override.

I might mull that over more and commit this piece first, saving directives for later.

text_import: Handle multiple byte groups

Have text2pcap and Import from Hex Dump support byte groups consisting
of 2 to 4 bytes in addition to individual bytes. By default assume
that byte groups are in network (big-endian) byte order, but add an
option to support little-endian byte order as produced by some hex dump

Also support "0x" or "0X" before the hex offsets, as produced by

Fix #16193
